doc.title: Buddy Burns and Frank Pasley Interview, 1968-09-23

chapter: Early career: New Orleans to Tulsa
title: Early New Orleans bands: Peter Williams, Jack Carey, Kid Punch, Arnold DePass
summary: He lists the New Orleans bandleaders he played with as a teenager, gives his 1904 birth, and names men in the Olympia band with Arnold DePass.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah. Did you have any other New Orleans musicians?
Oh, I played with Peter Williams. I played with Jack Carey. Jack Carey.
Yeah. And with Kid Punch. I played with Kid Punch when I was 16 years old. Oh, man.

I was born in 1904 in New Orleans, Louisiana. Which day? November 11th. Oh, yeah. And I played with the old, the old, the old Olympia band with Arnold De Pass. He's a drummer. He had a band around there. Oh, I think he played with Kid Punch too. Yeah. Well, they were much older musicians than me.
Excuse me. Who else was with you and Arnold De Pass in that band? Well, I can't call what.

They had one trombone player named Lewis and Herbert Mourney. Herbert Mouran. Herbert Mouran. Yeah, Herbert Mouran. Yeah. The Harlem band. Yeah. Let's see who else. I had a little fellow named Lewis played a clan that had been so long ago. I can't call all those. Not Josh Lewis? No. I never did play with George Lewis. Oh, yeah. I had left. See, I left New Orleans in 1924.
